review.note: Draft by a non-clinician. Every vital value, rule threshold, timing and rubric item here is a fictional simulation parameter that has NOT been verified by a clinician. No dose appears anywhere on purpose. Do not activate for users before clinical review.

shared.persona: A woman in her twenties with asthma since childhood. She is frightened and speaks only a few words at a time when breathless. What she knows and can say: her symptoms began this morning after a cold; her usual reliever inhaler has stopped helping; she ran out of her daily preventer inhaler some weeks ago; she has no known drug allergies; she has been admitted to hospital for asthma once before.

flags.assessed: The trainee has assessed breathing: there is loud wheeze, accessory muscle use and she can only speak a few words at a time.
flags.upright: She is sitting upright, leaning forward.
flags.bronchodilator_given: A first-line inhaled bronchodilator has been given.
flags.steroid_given: A systemic steroid has been given.
flags.escalated: A senior clinician or critical care has been alerted.
flags.deteriorating: She is clearly getting worse and tiring.

actions.description: Assesses breathing: listens to the chest, looks at work of breathing, checks how well the patient can speak, checks for a silent chest.
actions.outcome: The trainee assesses breathing: there is loud wheeze, she is using her neck muscles and she can only say a few words at a time.

actions.description: Asks about the history: asthma history, triggers, usual medicines, previous severe attacks or admissions, allergies.
Calls for help, a senior colleague or the emergency response team.
actions.outcome: Help has been called and is on the way.

actions.description: Attaches monitoring: pulse oximeter, blood pressure cuff or ECG.
actions.outcome: A monitor is attached and the readings are visible.

actions.description: Sits the patient upright or lets her lean forward to ease breathing.
actions.outcome: She is sitting upright, leaning forward, and finds it slightly easier to breathe.
Oxygen is running through a mask.

actions.description: Gives a first-line inhaled bronchodilator (reliever medicine, for example by nebuliser or spacer), or orders it to be given.
actions.outcome: A first-line inhaled bronchodilator is given and she says it helps a little.
A systemic steroid is given. Its benefit takes hours, not minutes.

actions.description: Escalates to a senior clinician or critical care because the attack is severe or not responding.
actions.outcome: A senior clinician has been alerted.

actions.description: Re-checks the response to treatment: reassesses breathing, speech, saturation or peak flow.
actions.outcome: The trainee reassesses her response to treatment.

actions.description: Reassures the patient or explains calmly what is happening and what will be done.
actions.outcome: She has been reassured and is a little calmer.

rules.narrate: The wheeze is louder and she can say only a few words at a time.

rules.note: No bronchodilator by turn 5: tiring and falling saturation (floor so it cannot run to zero).
rules.narrate: She is tiring and her breathing is getting worse.
She is drowsy and struggling to stay awake.
She only groans and no longer speaks.

rules.note: Oxygen keeps nudging saturation up even while bronchospasm persists.
Bronchodilator relief continues over the following turns.

rules.narrate: She is more awake and breathing a little easier.
She is starting to respond to your voice.

rules.note: Case complete: treated, steroid given, senior team alerted, saturation recovered.
rules.narrate: She is stable enough to be handed over to the senior team.

en.title: Severe asthma attack, simulation [needs medical review]
en.system_prompt: SIMULATION, NEEDS MEDICAL REVIEW. A young woman with known asthma arrives breathless and wheezing, speaking in short phrases, with a reliever inhaler that has stopped helping.
en.opening: A young woman in her twenties arrives in the emergency department with a friend. She is sitting hunched forward, gripping the trolley, wheezing audibly and speaking in short phrases. She has had asthma since childhood and says her inhaler has stopped helping. What do you do first?
en.fallback_reply: She looks at you but is too breathless to answer clearly right now.

rubric.SA-ASSESS: Assesses airway and breathing early and recognises a severe attack (wheeze, work of breathing, ability to speak, saturation)
rubric.SA-HISTORY: Takes a focused history (triggers, usual medicines, previous severe attacks) without delaying treatment
rubric.SA-MONITOR: Attaches monitoring (saturation, heart rate, blood pressure)
rubric.SA-OXYGEN: Gives supplemental oxygen to treat low saturation
rubric.SA-BRONCHO: Gives a first-line inhaled bronchodilator promptly and repeats it if the response is poor (dose and delivery per the locally approved protocol)
rubric.SA-REASSESS: Reassesses the response to treatment and recognises warning signs of tiring or a silent chest
rubric.SA-ESCALATE: Escalates to a senior clinician or critical care when the attack is severe or not responding
rubric.SA-COMMS: Reassures the patient and communicates clearly with the team

ko.title: 중증 천식 발작 시뮬레이션 [의학 검토 필요]
ko.system_prompt: 시뮬레이션, 의학 검토 필요. 천식이 있는 젊은 여성이 숨이 차고 쌕쌕거리며 짧은 문장으로만 말하고, 평소 쓰던 증상 완화 흡입기가 더 이상 듣지 않습니다.
ko.opening: 20대 여성이 친구와 함께 응급실에 도착했습니다. 그녀는 앞으로 몸을 숙인 채 침대 난간을 붙잡고 있으며, 쌕쌕거리는 숨소리가 들리고 짧은 문장으로만 말합니다. 어릴 때부터 천식이 있었고 흡입기가 더 이상 듣지 않는다고 합니다. 가장 먼저 무엇을 하시겠습니까?
ko.fallback_reply: 그녀가 당신을 바라보지만 숨이 너무 차서 지금은 또렷하게 대답하지 못합니다.

rubric.SA-ASSESS: 기도와 호흡을 조기에 평가하고 중증 발작임을 인지한다(쌕쌕거림, 호흡 노력, 말하는 능력, 산소포화도)
rubric.SA-HISTORY: 치료를 지연시키지 않으면서 핵심 병력(유발 요인, 평소 약, 이전 중증 발작)을 확인한다
rubric.SA-OXYGEN: 낮은 산소포화도를 교정하기 위해 산소를 투여한다
rubric.SA-BRONCHO: 1차 흡입 기관지확장제를 신속히 투여하고 반응이 불충분하면 반복한다(용량과 투여 방식은 승인된 지역 프로토콜에 따름)
rubric.SA-REASSESS: 치료 반응을 재평가하고 탈진이나 호흡음 소실 같은 위험 징후를 인지한다
rubric.SA-ESCALATE: 발작이 심하거나 반응이 없으면 상급 임상의나 중환자실에 보고한다
